WHAT_THE_SCOPE_NUMBERS_SUPPORT.a_peak_equal_to_the_cap_is_a_floor: 09-04's tape reported peak_bytes == max_bytes with 1,199 reclaims that pinned it there. That is a bound, not a measurement of demand: it supports `demand was AT LEAST the cap and was throttled 1,199 times`, and it is not commensurable with an unthrottled peak from another run
WHAT_THE_SCOPE_NUMBERS_SUPPORT.what_the_two_days_constrain: the builder's own footprint did not move (peak_rss_gb identical to three decimals across a 31% row spread, from a field that varies sensibly elsewhere); the whole cgroup difference sits in page cache, which ROSE on the smaller day as anon FELL -- so whatever differed was outside the builder's own allocation. Stronger than a correlation, weaker than a mechanism, and asserted as neither

ROW_ACCOUNTING.if_they_do_not_close: the residual is UNEXPLAINED and is reported as such rather than absorbed. Both sides are ROW counts and the total comes from round 58's receipt, not from this function -- so a mismatch is a real disagreement between producers, not a unit error
ROW_ACCOUNTING.population: FRAGMENT ROWS -- the rows phase2_arms reads from the day's fragment with status OK

UNCOVERED_GENERATIONS.population: REFERENCE GENERATIONS -- a DIFFERENT population from the row accounting above, which is why no reason breakdown is attached to it
UNCOVERED_GENERATIONS.superseded_field: reasons_account_for_the_count (round 59) -- withdrawn, not silently dropped: it compared rows with generations
UNCOVERED_GENERATIONS.why_no_reason_class_here: the drop classes (pre_window_excluded, gap_at_cutoff_excluded, no_level_history_excluded, state_join_failed) are counted in FRAGMENT ROWS. wrapper.a_SHARED_hold_does_not_satisfy_rule_20: rule 20 is ONE heavy run at a time. `flock -s` lets two holders in at once, and both would have read `held: true` under the previous two-conjunct test (REV 41)
wrapper.declared_wrapper_is_not_evidence: params carries a `wrapper` string; a string in a file cannot say what launched this process (R-575(C))

fresh_probe.why_two: a shared hold blocks an exclusive request and admits a shared one; only an exclusive hold blocks both. Rule 20 needs exclusivity

wrapper.how: a fresh-fd LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB that FAILS, AND a /proc/locks FLOCK entry on the lock's inode whose pid is this process or an ancestor -- the holder is the `flock` wrapper, not the python child
wrapper.lock_fd_is_corroboration_not_the_test: an fd on the lock file says the file is OPEN. Two lines of `open()` with no flock forged the old field, and a 1-hour / 6.84 GiB run certified itself (reviewer §2.3)
wrapper.why_mode_not_just_held: two `flock -s` holders would both report the fd and both certify; only WRITE is mutual exclusion

peak_censoring.not_comparable_to: an uncensored peak from another run -- a floor and a measurement are not commensurable, and differencing them reads as a demand difference that the numbers do not support
peak_censoring.what_this_peak_supports: demand peaked here and was never throttled; the peak is a measurement
